title: Pecan Pork Medallions with Apricot-Mustard Sauce
description: Thin, lean pork loin medallions poach under cover and are turned through a smooth apricot and Bavarian mustard sauce.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: boneless center-cut pork loin
ingredients.note: Intact, unenhanced loin with exterior fat trimmed.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: smooth apricot preserves
ingredients.note: Sieve out fruit skins or pieces.

ingredients.name: smooth Löwensenf Bavarian mustard
ingredients.note: Pass through a fine sieve if visibly grainy.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 275°F with pecan pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {ginger} and {garlic} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Slice the loin
steps.text: Cut {pork} across the grain into 3/8-inch medallions of even thickness.

steps.title: Cover immediately
steps.text: Arrange the medallions in a single layer in the smoked broth. Top up with {topup} if needed to just cover the meat, then fit the lid immediately. No stall wrap is needed.

steps.title: Poach the medallions
steps.text: Cook covered at 275°F for 8–18 minutes, checking early from the side. Remove each medallion to a covered dish with a little hot broth when its center reaches 145°F.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered pork off heat for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 3/4 cup into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Melt the preserves
steps.text: Stir {apricot} and {mustard} into the measured liquid over medium-low heat until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Coat and serve
steps.text: Lay the medallions in the apricot sauce and turn once. Fan them on the plates, spooning plenty of sauce over each piece.

notes: Make ahead: The medallions can be sliced and refrigerated the day before. Option A uses Bavarian mustard. For gentler Option B, omit the mustard and ginger and finish with a little more smooth apricot puree. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 234 kcal, 35.1 g protein, 13.7 g total carbohydrate, 4.6 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 150 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
